title: Grateful Dead Live at Springer's Inn on 1969-05-30
source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Ampex C-90) -> Dat (48k) D

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a classic late‑May ’69 show highlighted by a soaring Dark Star > Cosmic Charlie > St. Stephen > The Eleven marathon and tight band play.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller soundboard transfer is crisp and surprisingly clean for a 1969 tape, with only minor hiss and a brief cut at the end of “Turn On Your Lovelight.” Musically the performance shines – Jerry’s guitar roars on Dark Star, the band rides an epic sequence into Cosmic Charlie, St. Stephen and The Eleven, and the set is peppered with standout renditions of Doin’ That Rag, Morning Dew and Turn On Your Lovelight. Overall fans deem it a must‑have snapshot of the Dead at their psychedelic peak.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews, most giving 5 stars and praising both the music and the soundboard quality; only a few minor criticisms. Consistent praise for key jams and recording clarity yields a strong positive rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clear mix with slight tape hiss typical of ’69 tapes; occasional splice/cut at the end of “Turn On Your Lovelight” and a brief “screamer” during that track, but overall superior to most 1969 recordings.

poor_songs: "Cosmic Charlie" (one reviewer found the vocals terrible)
"Turn On Your Lovelight" (cut off at the end)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A classic late‑spring ’69 set: opening with Morning Dew, moving through Me & My Uncle and Doin’ That Rag, then launching into a 17‑minute Dark Star that segues into Cosmic Charlie, St. Stephen, The Eleven and finally Turn On Your Lovelight – an uninterrupted high‑energy jam marathon.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone described as “like his Gibson SG,” with an intense solo that builds midway through Dark Star; a broken string adds drama but he recovers powerfully.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass is called steady, sure‑footed and “thunderous” during the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal on Me & My Uncle noted as friendly and genuine; also contributes vocal texture on Lovelight.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart praised for near‑unison playing, dynamic interplay throughout the long sequences.
